holes_found.description: ISS-2456 PATCH INCOMPLETE — Part 5 ks-tldr (the kill-shot tab's TLDR, the most user-prominent surface in the entire kill-shot section) and Part 5 'Summary:' paragraph (idx 24828, end of Test 1 detail block) still say '78%' / 'failed by 78% on Sydney–Buenos Aires', while the same Part 5 Test 1 body's Problem 3 paragraph (idx 23509) now says '−73% error' / '3,194 km predicted'. ISS-2456 was closed at 17:35Z 2026-06-01 with resolution claiming 'Part5 → 3194km/-73%' but the patch only updated ONE of three 78% references in Part 5. The c2 h0 finding ('cross-section inconsistency on V12 SYD-BUE') is now an intra-section inconsistency within Part 5 itself. Per the curmudgeon.md TLDR rule ('TLDR factual errors are major because readers see TLDRs first and may not expand'), this is major. Defender risk: a reader expanding the Part 5 kill-shot tab sees the TLDR say 78%, the body math derive 73%, and the Summary recap revert to 78% — three numbers on the same page, all attributed to the same V12 formula on the same route. The cross-section harmonization is also broken: §7.1 TLDR and §6.10 both say 73%, but the Part 5 entry-point TLDR still says 78%.
holes_found.recommendation: Edit two strings in data/sections.json part5.html: (a) ks-tldr 'failed by 78% on Sydney–Buenos Aires' → 'failed by 73% on Sydney–Buenos Aires (dome acknowledges 25–78% range)' to match §7.1 TLDR's explanatory framing. (b) Summary paragraph '(3) failed by 78% on Sydney-Buenos Aires in V12' → '(3) failed by 73% on Sydney-Buenos Aires in V12' (or matching range framing). This closes the patch ISS-2456 intended to land. Defender-side counter-argument the operator should weigh: 'leaving the ks-tldr at 78% preserves the upper-bound shock value for casual readers; only readers who expand see the derivation.' Rebuttal: ks-tldr is the kill-shot — its purpose is to be the bluntest framing the review offers; numerical inconsistency within the kill-shot's own page is exactly the kind of error a dome defender would screenshot. Recommend opening a new ISS (or re-opening ISS-2456 with status 'verify-failed') to land these two sub-patches.

deeper_analysis: ISS-2456 was filed as a c2 h0 major finding: 'CROSS-SECTION INCONSISTENCY on V12 SYD-BUE error figure'. The c2 description explicitly enumerated four places saying 78% (Part 5 Test 1 body, §6.10, §7.1 TLDR) and one place (§7.1 body) deriving 73%. The decider self-patched at 17:35Z claiming 'Part5 → 3194km/-73%; §7.1 TLDR → 73%; §6.10 → 73%'. Forward-verifying with the current sections.json: §7.1 TLDR ✓, §6.10 ✓, Part 5 body Problem 3 ✓, but two additional Part 5 mentions (ks-tldr at idx 20773; Summary paragraph at idx 24828) were not in the c2 h0 enumeration and the decider did not catch them. This is a pattern worth flagging to tinker: c2 h0 enumerated 'Part 5 Test 1' as one site, but Part 5 Test 1 actually contains three sub-sites (ks-tldr, body, Summary) and the self-patch hit only one. A more careful enumeration would have used grep counts per page. Counter-argument the operator considered (per user preference): 'this is nitpicking — the decider got 60% of the patch right, and ISS-2457 is already on the docket to overhaul Part 5 Test 1 anyway, so the remaining 78% references will be swept up in that analyst expansion.' That's defensible, but ISS-2457 is moderate severity / assigned-analyst — it could sit for days. Meanwhile the kill-shot TLDR — the highest-traffic surface in the whole site — has a factual inconsistency RIGHT NOW that a dome defender could screenshot. Two-string edit, ~30 seconds of decider self-apply, closes the gap cleanly without waiting for the analyst expansion. Recommend not deferring. (Counter to my own counter: deferring is fine IF the ks-tldr+Summary are explicitly tracked in ISS-2457's scope. The current ISS-2457 description focuses on Antarctic rim / n(r) / structural-elements framing, not on number-harmonization. Add an addendum or open a separate fast-track ISS.) ISS-2459 patch is clean and complete — no comment.
